gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the ZowieREC 4K's '4K30' only applies to a 4K30 source: Zowietek's own support page says a 4K60 input, which is the default output of a PS5 or Xbox, is recorded at 1080p60. Of the listed recorders that take 4K60 in, only the ClonerAlliance UHD Pro and UHD Pro Max state they record that source in 4K (4K30).
standout_why: I compared against the cited rival pages and the other results ChatGPT got. ClonerAlliance's UHD Pro page (cited) says '4K@60fps video sources can be recorded at up to 4K@30fps'. The UHD Pro Max page gives only a 4K30 recording ceiling. AVerMedia's ER330 page (cited) and the RecDual page (cited) say 1080p recording while the 4K signal passes through. Streameez's HD PVR Pro 60 page (cited) has no recording specs. No Zowietek page was among ChatGPT's results, and in chat ab-32 ChatGPT carded the ZowieREC as 'Best affordable 4K recording … up to 4K30 … 4K60 passthrough'. Zowietek's product page also says 'up to 4Kp30' without the 4K60-source caveat, which appears only in its knowledge base. None of the results puts the recording ceilings (4K source behaviour, top bitrate, hours per card) on one common basis.
decides: For anyone recording a console or a PC at 4K60, the $199 ZowieREC records the same 1080p60 as the ~$130 Hauppauge HD PVR Pro 60, the $143.50 RecDual and the ER330. Only the UHD Pro ($278.50) or UHD Pro Max ($295.80) records 4K from that source, at 4K30, so they become the pick for 4K from consoles. The ZowieREC keeps its 4K edge only with 4K30 or 4K24 sources such as cameras. The HyperDeck Shuttle HD takes no 2160p input at all. At their top bitrates a 128 GB card holds about 5.7 h (UHD Pro, UHD Pro Max and ZowieREC at 50 Mbps), 9.5 h (RecDual at 30 Mbps) or 14.2 h (HD PVR Pro 60 at 20 Mbps).

findings.label: Recording from a 4K60 (or 1080p120) source
findings.source_title: Can it record 4K60 or 1080P120? – Zowietek Knowledge Base
findings.note: Maker FAQ: 'Yes, it supports 4K60 and 1080P120 input, with loop-out at 4K60 or 1080P120 … recording and streaming are downgraded to 1080P60.' The sister article 'Does it support recording 4k60?' gives the same answer. The full article body was partly cut off in my reader; the quoted lines are from the article and its knowledge-base category page.

findings.label: Maker's headline recording claim (the figure being normalised)

findings.note: The product page doesn't say what a 4K60 input is recorded at; that comes from the FAQ above. The disk formats are listed as 'FAT32 up to 2T, exFAT'. The default bitrate is 12 Mbps according to the maker's KB article 'How many KB/s does this record at?'

findings.source_title: HyperDeck Shuttle HD – Tech Specs | Blackmagic Design
findings.note: Maker: up to 157 hours of H.264 1080p59.94 on a 1 TB card. 1e12 B × 8 / (157 × 3600 s) = 14.2 Mbps, assuming a decimal TB. H.264, ProRes or DNxHD to SD/UHS-II or USB disks; exFAT/HFS+. Price $575.

findings.label: Hours per 128 GB card at each recorder's top bitrate
findings.value: 50 Mbps (UHD Pro, UHD Pro Max, ZowieREC) ≈ 5.7 h; 30 Mbps (RecDual) ≈ 9.5 h; 20 Mbps (HD PVR Pro 60) ≈ 14.2 h; 12 Mbps (ZowieREC default) ≈ 23.7 h
findings.source_title: Bitrates from each maker page cited above (UHD Pro, UHD Pro Max, ZowieREC, RecDual, HD PVR Pro 60)
findings.note: Arithmetic: 128e9 B × 8 = 1.024e12 bits; ÷ bitrate ÷ 3600. Video only: audio (up to 320 kbps on the UHD Pro) and file-system overhead are ignored, so real times are slightly shorter.

The cited datasheet PDF (EN_ER330_DS_20260618_TH.pdf) came back as unreadable binary and the PDF-to-text tool wasn't approved. I did not find a named reviewer with the figure.
ZowieREC maximum microSD capacity and file-split size: the product page and knowledge base don't state them (the 'How are video segments split?' article showed only its title).
File-split size for the ClonerAlliance UHD Pro, UHD Pro Max and RecDual: not stated on the maker pages.
